quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before you start the car, buckle your own seat belt. Make sure all passengers buckle theirs too. This should be part of your routine every time you drive.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead curves right first, then left. You should slow down so you can safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: You should always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. This includes changing lanes, turning into a parking space, leaving a parking space, pulling into traffic from an alley, and passing other vehicles.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other drivers.
Street lights.

questions.explanation: At night, pedestrians are harder to see than road signs and other objects on the side of the road.

questions.question: Alcohol affects your ability to:

options.text: Focus and concentrate.
Move and balance.
Think and make decisions.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They alert you to upcoming dangers. This sign warns that pedestrians may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to merge safely?

options.text: Use your mirrors and check your blind spots.
Speed up using the entrance ramp to match freeway traffic speed.
Let traffic already on the freeway go first.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up and match the freeway traffic. Yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before you merge to make sure you have room to enter safely.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Move to the right side and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, move safely to the right side of the road and stop. This gives the emergency vehicle a clear path. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly to the side when you can.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is always a very safe driver.
Always has the right of way.
Should not let other cars pass.
Can create a dangerous situation.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if cars are backing up behind you because you are driving too slowly, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and get ready to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic.
May go through the intersection if it is safe.
May not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May go through the intersection if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A steady green light allows you to drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, you must let other cars and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger tells you to stop.
There is a stop sign.
Flashing red lights and gates are working.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger or stop sign tells you to stop. Also stop when flashing red lights and gates are operating.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Keep going, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a steady green light, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection pass first. You can keep going, but slow down so you can stop if the light changes before you reach it.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps you drive safely?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid impaired driving is to arrange a ride with a friend who is not drinking. Coffee or a cold shower cannot reduce alcohol in your blood or its effects. It takes about one hour for your body to eliminate one drink.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, remember:

options.text: The road is very slippery right when rain starts.
Wet roads can cause your tires to lose grip.
Leave more space to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially when rain first starts. Water, oil, and dirt make the road slick. Slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush to keep your wheels from sliding.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep downhill ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: Bigger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that you cannot see in the mirrors.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is coming up.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave the emergency vehicle past you.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Let any emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren pass you, no matter which direction it is going. Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: Smoking while driving or getting ready to smoke:

options.text: Does not affect your driving.
Helps you stay alert.
Is a distraction.
Is not a distraction.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you by taking your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive no faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. High beams reflect light back into your eyes in fog, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are sitting in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in any vehicle on a public road or sidewalk.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of danger. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
More than 12 inches from the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, park within 12 inches of the edge.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect driving skills or judgment.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it harder to see clearly. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a lowering or raising gate at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, as long as a train is not too close.
Yes, if you do not damage the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.
No, never.

questions.explanation: When you see flashing red lights, lowered gates, or bells at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Do not cross until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Use the next exit and turn around there.
Ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the next exit and turn around there.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Continue to the next exit and turn around safely.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Continue to the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse.

questions.explanation: Do not make a quick turn if you miss your exit. Continue safely to the next exit.

questions.question: How should you safely cross a railroad track?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light flashes.
Listen and look both ways, then go if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is near.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways, then go if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Always listen and look both ways for a train from either direction before crossing. Only cross when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: You should slow down in which situations?

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not reduce alcohol in your system.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass another driver?

options.text: When next to a solid yellow line.
On a hill or curve in the road.
If oncoming traffic is near.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not pass when it could be unsafe for you or other drivers. Do not pass in no-passing zones, where you cannot see clearly, or when oncoming traffic is present.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds greatly increase the risk of death in a crash. Above 80 miles per hour, your chance of surviving a crash is very low. Driving slower than traffic can also be dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: Is signaling required before turning, changing lanes, or pulling from a curb?

options.text: Only if other traffic is nearby.
Yes. It is a good habit and the law requires it.
Only during the maneuver, not before.
Not if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle right or left. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before passing and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
Before returning to your lane, see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal 100 feet before passing. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Return to your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no traffic is crossing.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if there is no sign forbidding it.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for it.
Stop as fast as possible.
Slow down, move to create space for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to create space for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, slow down, make room for the emergency vehicle, and stop. Do not try to race the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Two-way left turn.
Minimum speed limit.
No parking.

questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must and must not do. Wherever this sign is posted, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, what should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and wait before moving forward.
Honk your horn and pass the bus on the left.
Keep driving once you think most children have left the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait before moving forward.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when a school bus has its stop arm extended. Do not move until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: When is it okay to pass on the shoulder of the road?

options.text: When the car in front of you is turning.
When the car in front of you is driving too slowly.
When you don't see any pedestrians.
Never.

questions.explanation: You are never allowed to drive on the shoulder of the road to pass another vehicle. Keep your vehicle on the pavement at all times.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both effects may become stronger.
Nothing will happen.
Both effects may become weaker.
Only the alcohol effects may become weaker.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects much stronger. For example, one drink mixed with a cold medicine could affect you like several drinks would.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Steer straight and slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas.
Keep your speed and drive straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer straight and slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep your car going straight. Remove your foot from the gas slowly. Do not use the brakes until you have control. Once the car is stable, brake gently and move to the side of the road safely.

questions.question: What should you do while in a travel lane on the road?

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may back up or make a U-turn if you miss the freeway entrance.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely leave the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Continue driving until you reach a safe place to pull off the road. If you miss a turn or exit, go to the next one instead of backing up.

questions.question: What can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Leaving extra time for your trip.
Following the posted speed limit.
Using your turn signals correctly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use your turn signals, follow speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on state highways when no other speed limit is posted?

options.text: 25 mph.
35 mph.
45 mph.
55 mph.

questions.explanation: The default speed limit on state highways is 55 mph. If a different speed limit sign is posted, follow that speed instead.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them away from crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely, even if your light is green. Be careful around pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: When can you pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street?

options.text: When you can clearly see the road ahead.
When you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
When your vehicle has the speed to pass safely.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe passing requires that you can clearly see ahead, return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle has enough speed to pass. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.explanation: Always reduce your speed when turning. This helps you control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to unexpected situations.
